t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup in Swiss International Typographic Style. A navy header band with a light wordmark. Below, a strict 4 by 2 grid of square-cornered near-square tiles edge to edge in a checkerboard of deep navy and warm limestone, hairline seams between them. Tiles carry huge light numerals with a slash, large light sans titles and either a small hairline table or a ruled list for <CONTENT>. One tile is a pale line blueprint of a storage tank on steel blue. Flat, no shadows.
signature_idea: Tank and pipework topics set as a Swiss checkerboard of slash-numbered tiles, with one steel-blue blueprint tank tile as the picture.
strengths: navy, limestone and one steel-blue tile are on-brand
huge light slash numerals give a strong Swiss rhythm
blueprint tile adds equipment context without 3D
tile grid maps to a token-only CSS grid
weaknesses: numerals are out of order and repeat (01, 02, 03, 03, 04, 01)
table text is garbled with invented values and misspellings
several tiles hold only a numeral with no content
mixes tiles, table and list with no clear reading order
lists heat exchangers and a steel-like tank, implying off-offer equipment
brand_fit_why: Palette, light numerals, square tiles and blueprint accent match the brand book, but empty and misnumbered tiles undermine precision.
